fatal_errors: The proposed sprayed nanoflake coating is unrelated to the target intervention of varying Mo content within SPS-fabricated CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composites.
The sole cited evidence concerns steel-on-steel testing at ambient temperature, so it does not support performance on HEA substrates from room temperature to 800 °C.
The claimed continuous, self-healing high-temperature glaze is not established by the cited evidence; oxidation or decomposition of the sulfide coating at elevated temperature is not addressed.
The generic untreated-HEA baseline prevents comparison with the target Mo0.2 composite and its measured temperature-dependent friction and wear.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general goal and proposes a genuinely testable alternative coating strategy. Its controlled ball-on-disk experiment, friction and wear measurements, surface analysis, and explicit falsification criterion are useful. However, it does not reconstruct the paper's compositional intervention, SPS processing, multiphase strengthening, or temperature-dependent MoS2/Ag and oxide–silver-molybdate lubrication mechanisms. Most importantly, E1 only demonstrates low friction and wear for an air-sprayed nanoflake lubricant on steel in ambient conditions. Extrapolation to bulk HEAs and 800 °C, including assertions of coating adhesion, self-healing, and glaze formation, is unsupported. Thus the idea is novel and experimentally discriminable but lacks valid evidence for its defining wide-temperature claim.
